title: Async instrumentation proxy sidecar for downstream trace normalization
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: We see fragmentation in how services and edge SDKs propagate trace metadata. Multiple clients (server frameworks, mobile SDKs, and language-specific SDK shims) use slightly different header names and sampling hints. This causes noisy/incomplete spans in downstream services and makes query joins brittle. Goal: build a small, deployable async instrumentation proxy (sidecar) that normalizes incoming request instrumentation into a canonical internal envelope, emits lightweight start/stop span events over a local fast channel (Unix socket / gRPC local), and forwards normalized headers to downstream services. The proxy should be optional for new services, backwards-compatible for existing SDKs, and introduce <1% p50 latency overhead for typical 50ms requests.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts incoming HTTP/gRPC/websocket connections and exposes a local Unix-socket gRPC endpoint for language SDKs to publish start/stop events.
On receipt, the proxy normalizes headers (case, common aliases, sampling hints) into the internal trace envelope and forwards normalized headers to downstream HTTP/gRPC calls.
End-to-end test shows <1% added p50 latency and <3% added p99 in synthetic 50ms request workload (baseline measured in lab).
Sampling reconciliation mode implemented: proxy can inject deterministic sample decisions and surface a diagnostic flag to downstream services when running sampling experiments.
Fallback behavior for non-instrumented clients: proxy inserts a lightweight trace root and preserves client ip/region tags for root attribution.
Integration tests + e2e dashboard widget demonstrating normalized traces for a 3-service transaction (edge -> service A sidecar -> service B).
Documentation: README, SDK adapters (Go/Node/Python) examples, and rollout playbook for canary to production.
comments: 2026-02-11 Aisha: Spike complete. Built a PoC that listens on unix:///var/run/redwood-instr.sock. PoC normalizes x-b3, traceparent, and custom X-RW-Trace into canonical envelope. Measured ~0.6% p50 overhead with local IPC + coroutine-based batching.

2026-02-18 Ben: Design review notes - add explicit header whitelist to avoid header bloat; prefer forwarding only the normalized header pair (rw-trace and rw-sampling). Also we should support a binary carrier for websocket frames later. Action: add whitelist and opt-in binary carrier flag.

2026-02-25 Infra: Deployment template for k8s sidecar added to repo under deploy/observability/sidecar.yaml. Uses an init container to create /var/run permissions. Needs secrets review (KMS) for signed provenance header.

2026-03-02 QA: Load test results attached. Under 1000 rps with 128B header sizes, p50 delta 0.4%, p99 delta 2.1% — passes target but p99 needs monitoring during real traffic shape. Added stress-case for 10k concurrent websockets.

2026-03-08 PM (Lena Park): Confirmed product intent — this enables SDK simplification and consistent dashboards. PM requests sampling-experiment mode to be feature-flagged per service. Added to rollout playbook.
2026-03-10 Security (Raj): Quick review - ensure normalized header is HMAC-signed if we include tenant attributes. Marked security_review_required. Gave pointer to KMS integration doc.
2026-03-12 Ben: Merged initial adapter for Node and Go under rwinstr/adapters. Opening PR for Python adapter next. Preparing canary on staging with the payment-service stack.
release_notes: Adds optional async instrumentation sidecar to normalize trace metadata and provide a local gRPC adapter for SDKs.
Provides sampling-experiment mode and header whitelist to avoid header proliferation.
Includes deployment templates and SDK adapters for Go/Node (Python forthcoming).
